items.name: Microsoft sours on neoclouds amid data center delays, costs (Bloomberg)
items.source: Bloomberg (Brody Ford) read in full via Yahoo Finance syndication, 2026-11-05 08:00 PST; Reuters pickup read via freedom969.com - reputable press, anonymous sources
items.headline: Microsoft sours on neoclouds amid data center delays, costs (Bloomberg)
items.candidate_dial: capex deferral / digestion + lease walk-away (principal: MSFT)
items.claim: Microsoft is tightening oversight of Nebius, IREN and Nscale projects, stepping away from ones it deems risky and debating internally whether to sign any new neocloud deals. Specifics printed: it cancelled a roughly $3bn Nscale UK (Loughton) deal in October over multiyear grid delays, declined to expand its Nscale Texas deal, walked away from a letter of intent to lease 1.35 GW in West Virginia, and agreed last week with IREN on a revised Texas timeline that may slip completion by several weeks or months. Microsoft says it added more than $200bn of data-center lease commitments over the last year and calls its practices normal; no formal policy change announced.
items.sweep_query: capex cut OR deferral OR digestion AI
items.note: Resolves (in part) yesterday's partial 456X Nov 5 item: this is the original report behind the 'declined Nscale capacity' line. Event dates inside the story: UK cancellation October 2026 (pre-gate, first detailed here); West Virginia LOI and Texas-option dates not printed. IREN and Nebius shares fell roughly 15-20% on 11-05. This is not a bond/loan deal pull and not an announced capex cut.

items.name: Microsoft declines option to expand Texas data center deal with Nscale, source says (Reuters, after FT)
items.source: Reuters (2026-11-05) read via Euronext Live syndication; FT original not read - reputable press, one anonymous source
items.headline: Microsoft declines option to expand Texas data center deal with Nscale, source says (Reuters, after FT)
items.claim: Microsoft will not exercise an option that would have more than doubled its Nscale Texas compute contract; the FT valued the extension at tens of billions of dollars. Per the source the decision was taken several months ago, before Nscale's September IPO filing, and leaves the existing contracts (up to about $43.8bn through December 2033; Nscale total contract value about $103bn) untouched.
items.note: Original report for the '~500 MW of Nscale capacity turned down' line in yesterday's partial 456X item; Reuters prints no MW figure (the ~500 MW figure appears only in the 456X briefs). as_of is the report date; the decision itself predates September 2026.

items.source: Bloomberg (Doan, Ford, Eckhouse) read in full via Insurance Journal syndication, 2026-11-05
items.headline: Bloomberg: AI data center boom set for upheaval after US election rout (~13 GW in Texas 'immediately exposed')
items.candidate_dial: GW deferral (analyst exposure estimates; no named cancellation)
items.claim: GLJ Research estimates about 13 GW of Texas data-center capacity is immediately exposed to the election result; projects with power but no state environmental permits could slip 12-18 months and those with neither may relocate. SemiAnalysis puts Texas at close to 30% of US capacity due online in 2028; about half of proposed US AI data-center additions could face stricter scrutiny. No cancellations named.

items.name: Pause pledges cover 41% of planned US data-center capacity (158.6 GW), all of OpenAI's pipeline (Cleanview; Bloomberg 11-06)
items.source: FourWeekMBA 2026-11-06 summarising Cleanview newsletter and a Bloomberg story dated 2026-11-06 - secondary
items.headline: Pause pledges cover 41% of planned US data-center capacity (158.6 GW), all of OpenAI's pipeline (Cleanview; Bloomberg 11-06)
items.candidate_dial: GW deferral (state-level pause pledges; exposure estimate, not enacted)
items.claim: Cleanview counts nine states whose governor or governor-elect has promised or imposed a data-center pause, holding 158.6 GW of planned capacity (41% of the US pipeline; Texas 88.4 GW, Ohio 21.9 GW, Georgia 20.2 GW), versus 56.7 GW under construction nationwide. Bloomberg Intelligence estimates 2027 AI infrastructure spending of $1.4tn could shrink roughly 5-7% and up to 10 GW might miss next year's schedule.
items.note: Updates the 37% figure in yesterday's The National item. Luminix report (read) adds that ballot measures directly blocked only about 1.6-1.9 GW of reported-size projects per Cleanview.

items.headline: WSJ: Anthropic IPO investors push valuation toward $1tn, suggest cutting raise to ~$80bn or delaying
items.candidate_dial: repriced round (AI lab IPO: valuation, size and timing)
items.claim: Prospective investors are pushing back on the planned $1.5tn IPO valuation: three said it will likely come down toward $1tn, one suggested shrinking the raise from up to $100bn to about $80bn and one raised postponing; Bloomberg separately reported discussions at roughly $1.4-1.5tn.
